extracted.subtask_description: Using the Manuscript Wish List Smart Search AI tool to find literary agents—how to craft queries, interpret results, and follow up with further research. Focuses on best practices for query wording (title vs synopsis, detail level), vetting returned agents, and using the tool as a starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a 2-paragraph synopsis
rubrics_metrics.description: My best results seemed to come from entering a 2-paragraph synopsis of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter a relatively detailed, two-paragraph synopsis rather than a short tagline or single-word comps; the author reports this produced the most aligned top results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and include details in your query
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agent Search box encourages adding more details; the search engine 'really appreciates a lot of detail' and gives positive feedback (green praise) when queries are detailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague, one-word or ambiguous queries — include genre, tone, narrative elements, point(s) of view, setting, and any distinctive traits so the tool can match more accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Try both comp title and synopsis searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Searching by a comp title returned different top results than searching by the comp's synopsis; you might want to try searching both by title and by synopsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a comp book identified, run one query with the comp's title and another with its synopsis — compare results because the tool may favor different agents for title vs. descriptive text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use generated tags to pick query keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: The tool generates tags for queries, which can be helpful for deciding which keywords to include in your query or to watch for in wish lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the generated tags as a source of useful keywords for your query letter or further searches; especially helpful when you use a synopsis as input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the word 'agent' to avoid editors in results
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever I didn’t include 'agent' in my query, editors sometimes popped up in the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add 'agent' (or similar filter wording) to your query if you specifically want agent matches rather than editors or other industry professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect inconsistency between runs — save results
rubrics_metrics.description: The same query run multiple times returned different results; the author noted receiving different top results on repeated runs and neglected to save all results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save or record result lists because repeated identical queries may yield different outputs; re-run queries and compare to assess stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run multiple variations of queries
rubrics_metrics.description: Different phrasings and combinations of elements (comp, synopsis, list of attributes) produced different top results; adding many elements without clarity can be vague but still useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try variations: short vs long synopsis, different comps, inclusion/exclusion of certain keywords, and re-ordering elements to discover different agent matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect the explanation/rationale for each recommended agent
rubrics_metrics.description: The details of why an agent was recommended (as shown in screenshots) can be particularly helpful to assess fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the tool's notes about each match — matching rationale can reveal whether the agent's expressed interests align with your manuscript's specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Smart Search as a starting point, then do your own digging
rubrics_metrics.description: The Smart Search is a great starting point, but writers need to do their own digging to ensure the agent truly aligns and is currently open to queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving matches, verify each agent via QueryTracker (QT), agency websites, wishlists, social posts, and recent deals to confirm fit and queryability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume an agent's absence means lack of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Just because an agent isn’t returned in the results, that doesn’t necessarily mean they wouldn’t be interested in your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A missing agent could be due to database coverage or algorithmic variance — include manual research and outreach when considering possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t expect exhaustiveness — the tool won’t list every agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Although there are a lot of agents listed here, you won’t find all of them here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the results as a sample of possible matches rather than a comprehensive agent list; supplement with other databases and networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good tool for writers who don’t know where to start
rubrics_metrics.description: For newly querying writers who have zero idea about agents they’d be interested in or even where to start, this is a much less intimidating starting point than QueryTracker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you're new to querying, use Smart Search to build an initial shortlist and reduce intimidation, but still follow up with vetting steps before querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware the tool can return non-agent industry professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors sometimes appeared in the results (e.g., top results included editors at St. Martins Press or Grand Central/Forever).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an editor appears, double-check the person's role; consider whether you want to target editors directly or refine the query to focus on agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the tool’s feedback cues to improve queries
rubrics_metrics.description: The search UI gives judgments (e.g., 'this query was pretty lame' or green praise) signaling query quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to the tool's feedback by expanding or clarifying your description when prompted to increase the chance of relevant matches.
